insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: The protocol has confirmed $1,087,101 in actual transactions across 17,563 receipts — deterministic purchase proof, not modeled intent. At $5+ CPM for probabilistic signals, brands are paying a premium for inference when cryptographically verified GMV data exists at scale.

Token acceleration crossed below 1.0x for the first time on May 1 (0.999x), meaning the slowdown is no longer just cooling — it is compounding. Weekly GMV has fallen from a $210,912 peak on April 13 to a $66K–$85K operating band, a 60%+ contraction in verified weekly commerce volume.

insights.topic: Intraday purchase pattern is stable and actionable
insights.insight: Across April 29–May 1, peak receipt inflow consistently occurs in the 16:15–20:15 window, with structural troughs at 00:15 as prior-week volume rolls off. For brands timing promotions or audience activation against verified buyers, this cycle is repeatable and measurable.

The network hit 29 active metros on April 19 — its highest count in observation history — with a single-heartbeat burst of 17 CBSAs at 81% diffusion rate. That footprint is now contracting to 20 active metros, signaling the initial expansion wave has peaked.

insights.topic: Digital commerce entering the receipt graph
insights.insight: Google appeared in the 14-day top brands list on April 28, the first digital-native brand in observation history, following SaaS subscriptions entering the category mix on April 9. The receipt corpus is no longer purely physical retail — digital spend verification is beginning to accumulate.

insights.topic: Lightning payout volume as proxy for engaged user quality
insights.insight: Only 257 Lightning payouts have been claimed out of 17,563 receipts, representing a small but self-selected cohort of users with active crypto wallets completing the full verification loop. For brands, this subset likely over-indexes on tech-forward, high-intent buyers worth isolating as a targeting segment.
